messages:
kavya: FYI — DSAR came in from an EU user asking for deletion of all derived embeddings and any search-index traces. Legal attached proof of request. Need a scope + plan. @liam can you confirm current storage + backup layout and whether we have a live delete path for snapshots? Also thinking about KMS considerations and auditability.

liam: quick summary: embeddings stored in s3 + postgres pointers, nightly backups to s3 Glacier + DB snapshots. Everything encrypted with kms key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111222333:key/redwood-embeds. Backups retention policy = 30d. We do not currently have an automated workflow to scrub historical backups for a single subject-id.

den a: legal's ask is full erasure. They said we need verifiable proof of deletion. They also warned against immediate deletion if there's an active legal hold. We need to confirm no hold.

kavya: ok — questions: 1) can we do targeted index scrub (remove vectors + metadata) + 2) crypto-shred backups (key rotation + schedule deletion) so data becomes unreadable? That may be faster than hunting every snapshot. Thoughts?

marta: crypto-shred is a reasonable approach but legal often wants an auditable trail showing actions taken. Key-rotation alone is defensible if we can show key lifecycle events and that no other assets rely on the key. Need infra signoff.

liam: agree. technical plan sketch: 1) redact embeddings for subject-id from live index and DB; 2) run a reindex to remove any residual search tokens; 3) schedule KMS key rotation + schedule deletion of old key. Example commands (high-level):

```
# remove user objects
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-embeds/users/9f3a --recursive
# DB: flag rows, then vacuum
psql -c "UPDATE embeddings SET deleted=true WHERE subject_id='9f3a';"
# schedule key deletion (after rotation window)
aws kms schedule-key-deletion --key-id <old-key-id> --pending-window-in-days 7
```

liam: note — schedule-key-deletion requires that the key isn't used by anything else, so must check IAM and bucket policies.

samir: RBAC note: Support and Solutions teams do not have permission to delete s3 objects in that bucket. I'm proposing a short-lived role 'dsar-deleter' with least privilege for the specific prefix, TTL 24h, and with mandatory approval flow in the console. That gives us an auditable, narrow blast radius.

dena: +1 to the temp role. Legal wants to see approver and timestamp in the audit log. Please make sure the role creation and assume events are logged to CloudTrail + our audit pipeline.

audit-bot: audit log created: dsar-1968452100 by kavya. events queued: evt-8921 (request received), evt-8922 (initial triage).

marta: decision proposal: do live deletion of embeddings and index scrub immediately, then proceed with crypto-shred of backups once legal confirms no ongoing hold. Create a retention-exception ticket to cover the interim period while we verify and execute.

kavya: agreed. Owners: liam = infra ops to run deletion + key orchestration; samir = RBAC + temp role; dena = legal coordination & signoff; marta = add runbook steps and update playbook. Target: EOD +2 (two business days).

samir: I'll prepare Terraform for the role + OPA policy and open a PR. Will include a one-click console approval UI that records approver identity.

dena: I'll draft a short legal confirmation template and will ping @legal-ops for sign-off once infra confirms the plan.

marta: I'll update the DSAR runbook with step-by-step commands (incl. verification hashes) and add a checklist for audit artifacts (:white_check_mark:). Also will add a Dashboard alert to flag residual tokens for that subject-id.

kavya: thanks all. If anyone hits blockers ping here. I'll create the JIRA ticket for the retention-exception and link infra + legal. Closing thread once owners confirm completion and attach audit bundle.

liam: noted. will post command outputs and CloudTrail links in the ticket after run.

samir: will coordinate rehearsals for the role assume flow tomorrow.

dena: tagging legal-ops for visibility: @legal-ops please standby for the confirmation doc.

audit-bot: audit log updated: evt-8923 (RBAC change requested).

kavya: :thumbsup:
